operating_characteristics: Point-to-point urban journeys; shared and individual service options; service tier can vary
fleet_management_characteristics: Driver/vehicle allocation is generally platform-mediated; the same vehicle may serve different trip purposes; no fixed route schedule is inherent to the model
available_evidence: Three-platform daily cab-trip estimate: approximately 1.62 million/day, derived from reported Uber (840k), Ola (460k) and Rapido (320k) figures
evidence_status: S-B/C-B estimate; daily values are source-reported and annualisation is a calculation
source_document: Motilal Oswal analysis; Business Standard, 18 Apr 2025
caveats: This is a three-platform cab-trip proxy, not a fully measured national ride-service total. Do not merge with the separate Redseer estimate. Trip-purpose split is unavailable.

demand_pattern: Demand is concentrated around flight arrivals/departures and airport pickup/drop-off periods; bookings can be scheduled or immediate
operating_model: Airport-focused operators and aggregators; airport operator controls access/concessions but is not necessarily the fleet owner
relevant_counterparties: Airport taxi operators; ride aggregators; airport concessionaires; passengers; airport operator
operating_characteristics: Airport-specific pickup processes, access rules and charges; pre-booked and walk-up services should not be treated as identical
fleet_management_characteristics: May involve dedicated airport fleets, aggregator supply, rank/queue allocation or pre-booked dispatch; third-party depot access and fleet access conditions are not established nationally
available_evidence: Evera listed by Delhi Airport for T3; OHM E-Cabs published a 100-EV RGIA deployment example in 2022; Delhi airport pickup fee reported at ₹290/trip in 2025
evidence_status: Presence/deployment examples documented; operator fleet metrics mainly company-reported; airport app-cab mode share not measured
source_document: Delhi Airport cab directory; OHM company presentation / EVJoints guide; ET/TOI 2025; DIAL blog Oct 2022
caveats: Airport passenger movements are not app-cab journeys or vehicle trips. National 20–30% airport app-cab mode share is an unsupported assumption. Pickup-fee incidence (passenger vs fleet) is unverified. Public charging on airport premises does not prove depot access for third-party fleets. Do not claim OHM is the only airport EV deployment.

booking_structure: Employer- or transport-service-contracted; scheduled in advance
demand_pattern: Recurring employee journeys, fixed shifts and routes, with demand shaped by client rosters and work schedules
operating_model: B2B mobility providers and contracted transport operators
relevant_counterparties: Employers; transport contractors; fleet operators; asset owners; drivers; charging providers
operating_characteristics: Recurring route and shift structures; enterprise service contracts; service quality and schedule adherence are important
fleet_management_characteristics: Often centrally managed with depot or captive charging arrangements; contract duration, renewal, payment terms and fleet ownership vary and are generally unpublished
available_evidence: Lithium Urban reports over 25,000 trips/day, more than 3,000 vehicles, 1,300 chargers and over 100 enterprise customers (June 2026); it separately reported about 300 km/day and 10–12 hour shifts in a 2025 interview
evidence_status: Company-reported (S-C); not independently audited. June 2026 vehicle total is not explicitly stated to be an all-EV count in the cited release
source_document: JSW Green Mobility press release, 25 Jun 2026; Mint interview, Jun 2025; Business Standard FY26
caveats: Do not label Lithium figures independently verified. Do not convert its 3,000+ vehicle network into 3,000+ EVs without a source confirming fleet composition. Contract terms and independently audited trip data are unavailable. Refex airport-to-B2B shift is one operator’s observed model change, not proof of airport-market unattractiveness.

booking_structure: Pre-booked point-to-point or scheduled inter-city service
demand_pattern: Trip-specific, lower-frequency demand with longer journey distances
operating_model: Platform-mediated inter-city products and independent charter operators
operating_characteristics: Longer distance travel between cities; operating requirements and charging access differ from urban use cases
fleet_management_characteristics: Vehicle allocation may be pre-booked or trip-specific; fleet control, return-load availability and charging strategy vary by operator
available_evidence: The market research does not establish a reliable India-wide inter-city cab volume or comparable vehicle utilisation dataset
evidence_status: Qualitative classification only; segment-level deck metrics are S-D/C-D and excluded
source_document: MARKET_STRATEGY_MASTER_RESEARCH.md; original deck segment table p3
source_reference: No independently verified segment-level volume or utilisation source identified in the supplied research
caveats: Do not use unsourced trip lengths, trips/day, fares, growth rates, EV shares or price-sensitivity values.
